intro: Here in İstanbul province stands a bronze column with a remarkable past: the Serpent Column, from 478 BC. The thirty-one Greek cities that beat Persia at Plataea cast it from captured weapons and dedicated it at Delphi. In the fourth century AD it was brought to the Hippodrome.
history: Its story begins with a victory. In 479 BC, thirty-one Greek cities beat Persia at Plataea. From the weapons they captured they cast this monument, and the following year, in 478 BC, they dedicated it at the temple of Apollo at Delphi. Eight metres of bronze, formed from three entwined serpents. In the fourth century AD it was brought to Constantinople and set up in the Hippodrome.
highlights: As you wander, don't miss the bronze shaft, the inscribed list of cities, the Hippodrome spina and a serpent head, now in the museum.
facts: Did you know? The names of the thirty-one cities that fought are cut into the shaft: the oldest list of a Greek alliance to survive. And the bronze itself is a trophy, cast from the weapons the thirty-one Greek cities captured when they beat Persia at Plataea.
outro: This brings our journey through the Serpent Column to an end. Before you go, a small request: please leave the stones untouched, keep to the marked paths and carry water with you. These stones have waited for centuries; let them keep waiting for those who come after you. Enjoy your visit.
